reviewed_by: Claude general-purpose subagent, blind judgment reviewer, post-fix stale re-review batch 5, 2026-08-02

samples_reviewed.question_text: Look at the 10×13 array. How many squares are shaded in all?
Shade all the squares inside the 2×63 rectangle. How many squares did you shade in all?

competency_fulfillment.rationale: Direct quotient items are arithmetically sound throughout — '300 ÷ 5 = ___' resolves to 60 and '165 ÷ 3 = 55. True or False?' correctly confirms the equation — but two of nine items, the '10×13 array' and '2×63 rectangle' tasks, key their answer to a product (130, 126) rather than any quotient, so those two never exercise the 'divide' verb the competency names.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: The competency names three explicit sub-cases, but 'with remainder' never occurs once — every division in the set resolves evenly ('300 ÷ 5 = ___'=60, '200 ÷ 4 = ___'=50, '20 ÷ 4'→5 for Ana's error) — and the '10,100,1000' sub-case only ever shows a divisor of 10 ('670 ÷ 10'), never 100 or 1000.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: Every stem stays a short single clause appropriate to grade 3 quarter 4, from 'What is 108 ÷ 2?' to the cloze '200 ÷ 4 = ___', with no compound or multi-part sentences layering extra reading demand onto the arithmetic.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: mcq, cloze, read_mcq, error_detect, set_fill_in_blank and true_false formatters all appear, but the read_mcq and set_fill_in_blank slots ('10×13 array', '2×63 rectangle') are multiplication-counting tasks rather than a genuine division variant, so real division-specific format breadth is narrower than the six formatter names suggest.

competency_alignment.rationale: The '10×13 array' (130) and '2×63 rectangle' (126) items ask students to count a product of two displayed dimensions, pulling two of nine samples onto array-multiplication rather than the division skill '300 ÷ 5 = ___' and '165 ÷ 3 = 55' correctly target.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: The competency's stated ceiling reaches 4-digit dividends divided by 100 or 1000, but the largest dividend anywhere in the set is 670 and no three-digit divisor case ever appears — the observed range (2- to 3-digit ÷ 1-2-digit) sits well under the node's own stated top end.
